questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chances of an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Do not look ahead. Focus only on your controls.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce accidents, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, hand signals are important. If the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with the palm facing back, all riders should stop.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should be all of the following except:

options.text: Made to meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no visible damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: If you are carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you on turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as they can without blocking your control of the motorcycle. They should hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is on the left handgrip.

questions.question: In a normal turn, what should happen?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays straight up.
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays straight up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays straight up.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can reduce your ability to ride safely. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than normal.
Start slowing down later than normal.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overworking the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than normal.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger in a sidecar changes how your motorcycle handles. You need more distance to stop completely.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: When should a group of riders merge onto a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: A staggered line is best for normal riding. However, riders should use a single-file line when going through curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should keep you safe. It should help you avoid blind spots, see and be seen, avoid road hazards, avoid wind from other vehicles, and give you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from entering your lane.

questions.question: What can happen if you shift to a lower gear without slowing down enough?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jolt and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jolt and a warning light may turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear too quickly, your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: What should your lane position help you do?

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Prevent other drivers from passing you.
Get to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your lane from other drivers and tells them what you plan to do next.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the most important thing is seeing the road behind and beside you.

questions.question: What causes more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who are new to their motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slowly release the throttle to slow down, and lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Height.
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol someone drinks, how fast they drink, and body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: What is the best group formation when riding through curves, turning, or entering a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: A staggered line is usually best for group riding. However, use a single-file line when going through curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrower view so you can focus better.
You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
You can follow the next vehicle's path more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move if needed.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do if someone tailgates you?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up and put distance between you and the tailgater.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass you. Speeding up can be dangerous. It may encourage them to follow at an even faster speed.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: When going through curves or turns, motorcyclists should ride in single-file. This also applies when entering or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is used on straightaways.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
Is better than riding behind the other vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside another vehicle can put you in the driver's blind spot. The driver may not see you and could hit you. Also, if a hazard appears, you have no escape route.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, slow down as much as possible before impact. Keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel just before hitting it.
